div.p: Khairabad is an ancient town of immense historical, intellectual, and spiritual significance situated 8 km south of Sitapur district headquarters on National Highway 30 (Lucknow–Delhi highway). The town was founded in the early 11th century and later served as the head of an administrative Sarkar under Emperor Akbar in the Subah of Awadh.

The town is world-renowned for its intellectual contributions to philosophy and Islamic jurisprudence, being the birthplace and ancestral seat of the great 19th-century scholar and freedom fighter Allama Fazl-e-Haq Khairabadi. Khairabad also reflects India's rich composite culture, housing both the historic 17th-century Hindu complex of Badi Sangat Mandir and revered spiritual Sufi shrines such as Dargah Hazrat Makhdoom Sheikh Saaduddin and Dargah Qadam Rasul.
